summary_out.changed: Replaced vol-regime-sizer's fast/slow volatility-ratio gate with a choppiness-ratio gate (path_length / displacement on a 30-tick window); skip probability decays exponentially when chop_ratio exceeds 1.5, separating whipsaw regimes (high chop) from trending breakouts (chop near 1.0) that the magnitude-only base treats identically.
summary_out.outcome: pnl +34.13% vs vol-regime-sizer (1011.0 vs 753.75), sharpe 5.97 vs 3.06, max_drawdown_pct -0.0420 vs -0.0460 (tighter), trade_count -14.5% (109424 vs 127991), win_rate -0.0056 (0.3473 vs 0.3529); mean_slippage 0.0 on both sides (sim fills at top-of-book — slippage delta undefined, reported as 0.0); is_weighted_bps marginally worse (+0.0047) — gains come from skip selection, not per-trade execution quality.
summary_out.hypothesis: Whipsaw regimes (where consecutive ticks reverse) drive a disproportionate share of oracle losses; the base sizer's magnitude-only fast/slow ratio cannot distinguish them from directional breakouts and skips both. A path-length/displacement ratio identifies whipsaws while leaving trending motion untouched, preserving adverse-day savings AND recovering forfeited directional upside.
summary_out.next: Combine chop-gating with island-0's spread-quantile gate (they should be near-orthogonal — chop measures whipsaw frequency in price space, spread measures liquidity-vacuum risk in book space); separately, add a trend-strength reinforcer (signed sum of delta_mid) so confirmed trends LIFT p_submit instead of just not skipping them; calibrate chop_neutral/sensitivity per session since chop's natural scale tracks realized vol.
